case_title: P. NAGESH AND ANOTHER V. STATE OF KARNATAKA
trial_court_outcome: convicted under Sections 364, 302, 379, 201 read with Section 34 of the IPC and sentenced to undergo imprisonment for life
neutral_facts: The prosecution relied on circumstantial evidence to prove the guilt of the accused. The evidence included the accused being found in possession of a motor cycle that had been used by the deceased, the discovery of the dead body at the voluntary instance of the accused, the exhumation proceedings leading to the discovery of the buried dead body, and the identification of the dead body by the victim's family members. The medical report indicated that the death could have been caused by strangulation by a rope. The accused challenged the prosecution's evidence, arguing that the recovery of the motor cycle and the dead body was false, the police had visited the location prior to the exhumation, and the cause of death was not established beyond reasonable doubt. The prosecution failed to prove the recovery of the motor cycle and the wrist watch of the deceased, and the witnesses did not withstand cross-examination.
